sequestro: You never saw where it came from.
A thick cloth over your head. A yank that lifts you off your feet.
Back of a van. Oil, cigarettes, the hot exhaust against your back. A hand pinning your neck down the whole way.
They brake. They drag you out by the collar.
They rip the cloth off in one pull — and the light burns your eyes. Wire mesh on both sides. And a roar of people that won't stop growing.
venceu_blocos: Last one standing is you. The whole pit saw it.
Nato walks in hard, takes the book and tears it page by page in your face.
Then he counts {premio} into your hand. They blindfold you again. You wake up on some corner of the Track — body aching, name back to zero.
venceu_blocos_grana: Nato counts {premio} into your hand. Dry, without looking at you.
You got nothing else — nobody leaves the pit smarter, just more marked up. They blindfold you, dump you on the Track with a heavy pocket.
perdeu_blocos: The pit floor came up fast.
You wake up later: mattress on the ground, taste of blood, somebody closing your brow with sewing thread.
Nato doesn't even show. He sends word through the muscle.
«The buy-in is debt. And the pit never closes.»
fuga_blocos: Jumped the wire mesh before the next one and slipped into the street.
Nato's book is yours now, fat as it got.
«It finds you. At any bar. In any hood.»

combat_tutorial.iniciativa: That track up top shows whose turn it is: everyone runs to the center and acts on arrival. More Pace gets there first and acts more — up to 3 actions to the slowest one's 1.
combat_tutorial.escolher_alvo: More than one enemy? Tap whoever you want to attack to pick them as your target — kill the weakest first or focus the strongest, your call.
combat_tutorial.bolinha: That little ball is your menu (drag it to any corner). ATTACK costs nothing; TALENT spends PM and shows what it does — a Hexer's can leave a status on the target; ITEM uses a potion or a status cure.

alvo_tutorial.farol: Check the dot colors: red is required to open the way, yellow is optional (pays cash or items) and green is done — if it was a repeatable fight, you can come back and farm it. Walk up and the action opens by itself.

ko_tutorial.aliado: An ally went down? They're out for the rest of the fight, but the rest of your crew keeps swinging. Keep an eye on everyone's PV.

xp_tutorial.regra: Fight points aren't split evenly: whoever finishes off the most takes the biggest share. Beating someone way weaker than your strongest pays little (never under 5); taking on someone stronger pays double or triple.

descanso_tutorial.recuperar: Here the crew rests: 10 heals whoever's standing, 30 gets the downed back up too, and 50 is the full job — health, downed and status. Status only goes away here or with a cure.

agiota_tutorial.emprestimo: Short on cash? The loan shark lends — but you pay back 10x as debt, and every credit heal after that DOUBLES what you owe. Hit the ceiling and he heals you free, then throws you straight into the Fight Club to settle up.

clube_tutorial.como_funciona: The Fight Club is a betting pit: 3 rounds back to back, no rest. Win and you clear the debt AND take the neighborhood's cash; lose and they patch you up — it doesn't count as a real loss. But the buy-in comes on credit.
clube_tutorial.cura_dobra: Between rounds you can patch yourself up — but healing again DOUBLES what you owe. Running mid-fight keeps the debt as it was.

story.world_hint: Tap a region on the map
story.facil_ultimo: You REALLY think you're going to face the last hood's boss playing on EASY? He won't even stoop to look at you. On easy you get to the 6th and that's it — whoever wants the top plays for real. Bump it to Medium at least, kid.
story.confronto_final: The one who almost made it
story.precisa_informante: 🔍 Before you face the Feira's heavy, go back to the Pista and have a word with Duda. He knows things worth gold.

fumaca.fala: You quick, kid? I'm smoke. Blink and I'm already gone — and you eat it in the dark without even seeing where the hit came from.

turco.fala: All of Marélia owes me. Now {suaGangue} does too. Round here, whoever can't pay in cash pays in bone.

espeto.fala: Good coffee. Been a long time since I woke up like this. You beat my boys and sent Peacock running… Fine. Now come take the Lowside, if you can handle it.

sala.fala: Climbed ten floors just to get dropped on the last one? Respect the effort. Changes nothing.

zefa.fala: I raised half the kids {suaGangue} beat to get up here. Sit down. Your punishment's gonna take a while.

doutor.fala: Do the math, kid. You've got two fighters. I've got the whole Hilltop owing me favors. Now go home.

costura.fala: All of Marélia was mine once. Six blocks in hand, the Rooftop under my feet. But this thing won't stitch — not even I held it. Come up here and I'll show you the hard way.

pista.desc: The raw asphalt down below. Kids chasing chains, selling gum, eyes everywhere. Rato de Pista with no big dreams, Bonde do Sinal cashing in on information. Nobody heavy yet — but every flag holder walked here first. The Patchwork did. A kid named Alan will walk it too, somewhere else — his turn just hasn't come yet. Now it's your turn.

feira.desc: The stalls, the vendors, the spliced power lines. No shooting here — just debt. The Collector writes it all down, and the Collector collects it all.

baixada.desc: Across the train tracks. The Shadow's crew split three ways when he died. Crimson, Cold and the Leftovers bite each other before they bite you.

vila.desc: The blocks, the ten-floor towers, the unlit stairwell. The crew runs it bottom to top. To reach the owner you climb it all taking hits.

morro.desc: The hillside slum, the concrete stairway that changes shape with every new rooftop. The spots, the firework boys. Nobody comes down the Hill the same.

alto.desc: Past the steel door. The Five nearly became a council — pulled half the Hill into one hand before the Patchwork came, and before you.

laje.desc: The top. On one side, all of Marélia watching. On the other, the Patchwork — the only one who ever held six blocks at once. This is where you find out if seven can be held.

falas.ponto: {territorio}. This spot belongs to {gangue}, pal. {suaGangue} doesn't walk through here for free.

paragrafos: {gangue} put the Patchwork down on the Rooftop. All of Marélia saw it.
And then you understood what he already knew. Two weeks and the map was split again — blocks pulling one way, spots pulling another. Nobody holds this city. He didn't. You didn't.
Years later a kid with weird hair would do what neither of you could. His name was Alan. But that's another story — and you're in it, right at the start.

modes.dif_facil_desc: The crew comes in weak. But on easy you get to the 6th hood and stop — the last boss won't stoop to face a kid. Want the top? Bump it to Medium.
modes.dif_medio_desc: The way it was designed. The crew comes at your level and Carvão will see you. For real ones.
modes.dif_dificil_desc: The crew comes with almost everything you've got, and Carvão still brings backup. For those who don't cry.
modes.historia_desc: Climb the Hill. Take Marélia one step at a time — every turf up to the boss, progress saved.
modes.batalha_desc: A quick 2×2 fight against the opponent you pick. No map progress.
modes.batalha_bloqueada_toast: Not yet, kid. The Tower only opens once you crack Marélia wide open — all 7 turfs, end to end, up to planting your flag in Laje.
modes.multiplayer_bloqueada_toast: That one's tough, kid. Only unlocks once at least 3 of your crew maxes out — level 99. Get grinding.
modes.multiplayer_liberado_toast: Look at that, your crew's already got 3 sheets maxed out. The online run against other gangs is ready to go — just waiting on the update.

batalha.sub: Fight after fight to level up fast. Your gang is at average level {n}.

folga_desc.leve: Well below your gang — safe farming.
folga_desc.igual: Your gang's size — a fair fight.
folga_desc.puxado: Above your gang — more AP, more risk.
folga_desc.brabo: Way above — to see how far you can go.

naming.poster_pitch: Every street knows a name. Choose the one all of Marélia learns to respect — or to fear.
naming.label: Gang name
naming.placeholder: e.g. End of the Line Crew
abertura: So you're thinking about starting a gang, huh? Think you can hang with Marélia's heavy hitters?

Careful what you wish for, kid. Up there are people who've swallowed whole flags for breakfast. The Patchwork once held six blocks in one hand — and you're here, out of nowhere, thinking it'll go different for you.
Fine. Just don't go nameless. A street name becomes a legend or a joke — and it's the one they'll spit back in your face when you're on the Rooftop, face to face with the real deal. Choose wisely.

dialogo.veio_sub: the corner elder, owner of the bar

chegada: This is the Rooftop, kid. The top. On one side, all of Marélia. On the other, the Patchwork.
He's the only one who ever held six hoods at once. He treats crime like a spreadsheet, and every hood is a thread stitched in his hand.
You're gonna meet people you already took down up here. They climbed up for revenge — and now they hit at Rooftop level.
And pay attention: as long as his threads stay stitched down below, he won't go down easy. Up there nobody helps you. Climb with what you brought.
laje.aviso_informante: Nobody on the Rooftop will take you to the Patchwork yet. There's a message for you at the Hilltop Bar — hear it first.
laje.checklist_dica: Get through the stitched entrance, the sewing room, and climb to the top. And cut the Patchwork's threads in the hoods below — every one left makes him stronger.
laje.checklist_passagem: The way is open. Climb to the top of the Rooftop and end this.
laje.linhas_sobram: {n} thread(s) still stitched: +{n} Wallop and Hide on him

encarar.label: Settle it with your fists
encarar.resultado: "Then come on. But know this: whoever gets beat by you goes crying to the Accountant."

cinco_quarto.sub: the closest to becoming a real council
fala: We were one name short of being a council. Just one.
Eight hundred. Or you find out why they call me general.

comprar.label: Buy out his debt (800)
comprar.resultado: You count the cash in front of him. He crosses his own name out of the Accountant's book. "Now I owe you."

encarar.label: Settle it with your fists
encarar.resultado: "Then come on. But know this: whoever gets beat by you goes crying to the Accountant."

roda.sub: the formation that trains for the Five
fala: Nobody fights alone here. Not us, not you.
Step into the circle. Whoever holds up walks out.
The Five were the head. I'm the body.
You want the Accountant? He's on the other side of my formation.

favor_devido.sub: owes the Accountant, fights to pay it off
fala: Every guy I drop is one month off the book.
You're worth three months, at least.

rinha_alto.sub: endless fights with a view of all of Marélia
fala: The Hilltop ring has the best view in the city. And the worst hits.
One ends, another steps in, random. You can leave the crew here — 1 fight every 5 minutes.

birosca_alto.sub: fake whiskey and torn leather chairs
birosca_alto.intro: Up here even the bar thinks it's a council. But the crew rests the same. Costs a little.

fala: Need cash? The Accountant always has some. And always writes it down.
1200 in your hand now. The math, the Accountant does.
divida_do_alto.contrato_corpo: "1200 in hand, right now. Take it or leave it?"
divida_do_alto.contrato_letra_miuda: Fine print: you end up owing {divida}.

emporio.sub: the best stuff that makes it up the Hill

ferraria_alto.fala: We forge the steel door here. Bring the piece and some scrap and I'll get it right — up to +8.

mesa_dos_cinco.sub: where they almost became a council
mesa_dos_cinco.linha: Five chairs, one empty. In the drawer, a little cash and a bottle of syrup nobody had the nerve to take.

jogo_porrinha.fala: "Sit down, kid. Before the beating, we play. Everybody knows how to fight. Hardly anybody knows how to count."
jogo_porrinha.regra: Each of you has 3 sticks. Hide 0 up to what you have and guess the total of both hands. Whoever guesses the total throws one stick away. First to run out wins.
jogo_porrinha.ganhou: "Hm. You count right." He pushes his chair back and points to the back door. "Pool. Come on."
jogo_porrinha.perdeu: "See? The math always works out in my favor." He shuffles the sticks again. "Another one? I've got all night."

jogo_bilhar.fala: "Three balls, six pockets. I did it in five shots. You get six. Fair, right?"
jogo_bilhar.regra: Drag your finger back from the cue ball to aim and set the power, then let go. Sink all 3 balls in 6 shots or fewer. A scratched cue ball goes back to its spot and costs the shot.
jogo_bilhar.ganhou: He claps slowly. "Nice. Now we're talking." He takes off his jacket and folds it on the table. "Now we do it the way you like."
jogo_bilhar.perdeu: "Ran out of shots, kid." He racks the balls again. "Chalk up and try another."

fala: The Accountant says: whoever took down Zefa can come up to the Hilltop.
But up there everything has a price. And the Accountant knows everybody's price.

ouvir.label: Take the message
ouvir.resultado: The kid disappears behind the steel door. Now the Hilltop knows you're coming.

chegada: This is the Hill, kid. Nobody ever took this place. Not even the Patchwork.
Zefa doesn't sell the Hill, she negotiates it. And the Firework Boys lock the stairway with three gates.
Every gate has a price, and you don't pay it up here: you pay it down below, in the hoods you already got in your pocket.
Go back to the Track, the Market and the Lowside and negotiate your way up. Up here, your word is what counts.
morro.aviso_informante: Nobody on the Hill will take you to Zefa yet. There's a message for you at the bar in the Projects — hear it first.
morro.checklist_dica: Climb the stairway. Gate locked? The pass is in a hood down below — the Track, the Market and the Lowside, in the bar's back room.
morro.checklist_passagem: The stairway is open. Walk into Zefa's den.

barreira.pista: GATE LOCKED · the pass belongs to Hornet, back on the Track
barreira.feira: GATE LOCKED · the Firework Boys want radios — negotiate at the Market
barreira.baixada: GATE LOCKED · the daycare needs medicine — negotiate in the Lowside

fala: From here up you need a pass. And you got none.
Every step here has an owner, pal.
I eat the stairs from the inside. You'll fall before you notice.
Whoever climbs without asking comes down rolling.
Yesterday this was an alley. Today it's a slab. Tomorrow it's your grave.
Stairs move around here, and you don't know a single one.

posto_rojao.sub: the alarm for the whole Hill
fala: One bang and the whole Hill knows you came up.
Short fuse, even shorter patience.

segunda_mae.sub: watches the kids when Zefa can't
fala: I changed diapers for half this crew. You think I'm scared of you?
Hit hard, and I'll hit back with love.
You negotiated the gates down below. With me there's no deal.
I am the stairway. Climb over me, if you can.

ultima_escada.sub: the last step before the den
fala: From here you see the whole Hill. And it sees you falling.
One more step and you're in front of Zefa. You won't make it.

conta_do_morro.sub: keeps track of who owes Zefa a favor
fala: Your name's in the book. Everybody who climbs is.
Zefa only sees people whose tab is paid up.

morador.nome: Resident at the foot of the Hill
morador.sub: watched the Hill grow slab by slab
fala: The Firework Boys lock the stairs in three spots. Iron gates, thick padlocks.
Hornet on the Track charges a toll to anyone who wants to go up. He and Zefa go way back.
The Firework Boys always have broken radios. Whoever finds valves at the Market wins them over.
Zefa's daycare never has enough medicine. Whoever sends some from the Lowside, she won't forget.
The Patchwork almost took everything. The Hill he never took. Zefa just sat down and talked.
Nobody climbs here by taking beatings. Here you climb by making deals.

rinha_morro.sub: endless fights with a view of the Hill
fala: The Hill's ring is on the highest slab, with the whole hood watching.
One ends, another steps in, random. You can leave the crew here — 1 fight every 5 minutes.

birosca_morro.intro: The owner sets the crew up in a corner and makes everybody eat. Costs a little and nobody leaves hungry.

fala: Need something, kid? On the Hill, money comes with a favor attached.
1000 in your hand now. The favor... Zefa picks the favor later.
fiado_da_zefa.contrato_corpo: "1000 in hand, right now. Take it or leave it?"
fiado_da_zefa.contrato_letra_miuda: Fine print: you end up owing {divida}.

venda.sub: whatever comes up the stairs, she sells

serralheria_morro.fala: We weld the Firework Boys' gates here. Bring the piece and some scrap and I'll get it right — up to +7.

fala: Nobody fights in here. Not you, not them. It's the one rule Zefa never negotiated.
Zefa raised half the Hill in this room. The same kids you beat on the stairs.
She never forgives anyone who messes with kids. And she never forgets who helps.

creche_achado.linha: In the donation box, somebody left a little cash and a bottle of syrup. The daycare lady says it's for you: "whoever helps the daycare, the daycare helps."

fala: You wanna climb the Hill? Heh. Zefa owes me an old favor, and I owe her another.
Six hundred in my hand and I'll have the first gate opened. It's not a loan, kid. It's a toll.

pagar.label: Pay the toll (600)
pagar.resultado: He pockets the cash, picks up the phone and says two words. "Go on up. The first gate is open."

fala: The Firework Boys up on the Hill have busted radios. No radio, and fireworks are useless.
Get me three valves and I'll send them up, and they'll open the second gate. The street vendor has them.

entregar.label: Hand over the 3 valves
entregar.resultado: "Deal. The radios will crackle again and the second gate will open for you."

aval_morro_baixada.sub: Dona Lurdes knows the daycare lady
fala: Zefa's daycare has been out of medicine for weeks. The lady called me crying.
Get me two Bone Potions, the ones from the Projects, and I'll take them myself. Zefa opens the last gate for whoever helped her kids.

entregar.label: Hand over the 2 Bone Potions
entregar.resultado: She wraps the potions in a dish towel. "Zefa's gonna know it was you. The third gate is open."

informante_morro.sub: a kid from the Stairway Front
fala: Zefa says: whoever took down Rust can climb the Hill. But on the Hill you don't climb by taking beatings.
The stairway gates only open with a pass. And the passes are down below, in the hoods you already own.

ouvir.label: Take the message
ouvir.resultado: The kid disappears down the stairs. Now the Hill knows you're coming — and so do the hoods below.

chegada: This is the Projects, kid. Three blocks, ten floors each, and a stairwell with no lights.
The war here runs bottom to top: the Tower Crew holds the ground floor and the stairs, and the Upstairs folks live way up high.
The owner is Rust, on the rooftop. To reach him you climb floor by floor, taking hits on every landing.
And watch out for the Front Desk: he runs ahead warning the crew. The more you lose, the readier they wait for you.
vila.aviso_informante: Nobody in the Projects will take you to the rooftop yet. Dona Lurdes, at the bar in the Lowside, knows the way — hear her out first.
vila.checklist_dica: Climb Block A: beat whoever holds each floor, all the way to the rooftop.
vila.checklist_passagem: All ten floors are clear. Go up to the rooftop and face Rust.
vila.hint_elevador: Dona Neide, on the 5th floor, has the elevator key. With it you go up and down without redoing the stairs.
vila.grafite:
WHO GOES UP
DON'T COME DOWN

alerta.sobe: the crew is warned: +{n} on each of them

fala: The car creaks, the light flickers. Smells like burnt oil and trouble.
Sometimes it stops halfway. And whoever's waiting outside isn't there to help.
elevador.travou: The elevator got stuck between floors! The doors get pried open — and the crew is right outside.

guarita.sub: the front gate of the Projects
fala: Resident? No. Visitor? Nope. Then you ain't coming in.
Here the crew decides who goes up. And the crew said no.

portaria_fuga_1.sub: ran to Block A yelling into his radio
fala: Come in, come in, someone's coming up! Someone's coming up!
Hold this guy while I warn the folks upstairs!
You wanna get through that gate? Only over my body.
The key to Block A is in my pocket. Come and get it.
Down here in the dark, I'm the one who sees.
You trip, you fall. You fall, you get beat.
You can't even find the next step and you wanna fight?
Every floor has an owner. This one's mine.
Two floors up and you're already sweating. Eight to go.
Nobody gets through here without opening the deadbolt. And the deadbolt is me.
You again?! Guys, he's on the fourth floor!
I call it in, they bring the beating. That's how it works here.
You're behind on your fees, visitor. The fine goes on your face.
The janitor here works for us. Got it?
Okay, okay! But if you get past here, I'll never warn anybody again!
This radio's all I got, kid. Don't break it...
You climbed seven floors to find me? Feel the weight of the block.
I'm the wall that keeps this building standing.
Drips slow, but never stops. Just like me.
From here up it's another level, punk. We pay for our lights.
Every door in this building opens with my key. Except the rooftop.
You came far. But far ain't the top.

apto_801.sub: the janitor posing as a tenant
fala: I've lived here twenty years. Nobody ever knocked on my door like that.
You weren't supposed to see my uniform under the bathrobe.

vizinho.sub: loud music and a louder mouth
fala: Rust never comes down. They say he hasn't touched the ground floor in ten years.
The elevator? Breaks every week. But the crew fixes it real quick when it's time for an ambush.
The Upstairs pay for the lights in their stairwell. The one down here stays dark on purpose.
Dona Neide on the fifth is the only one the crew respects. She raised half of them when they were kids.
Front Desk is scared of everything. But his radio is what holds this building together.
Whoever climbs here gets tired. And Rust is counting on that.

varal_patio.linha: In the pocket of some pants left on the line: a little cash and a bottle of syrup.

apto_302.linha: Feeling around in the dark, you find a bandage and some cash on the floor.

apto_604.linha: On top of the fridge: a bottle of bone potion and a little cash.

rinha_laje.sub: endless fights up on the slab
fala: The Projects' ring is up on the slab, with the whole building watching from the windows.
One ends, another steps in, random. You can leave the crew here — 1 fight every 5 minutes.

birosca_vila.intro: The owner sets the crew up in a corner, away from the stairs. Costs a little and everyone walks out whole.

dona_neide_descanso.intro: Dona Neide puts the crew on the couch, brews some coffee and scolds everybody. Costs a little — and nobody leaves without eating.

dona_neide.sub: the only one the crew respects
fala: Made it to the fifth, huh? The whole building's talking about you.
Here, the elevator key. My knees can't take these stairs anymore, and yours won't either.

pega_chave.label: Take the elevator key
pega_chave.resultado: She takes the key off her neck and hands it over. "Careful, it gets stuck. And when it does, it's no accident."

fala: Need cash, visitor? In the Projects everything has rent. Even money.
800 in your hand now. The due date... I decide the due date.
aluguel_vencido.contrato_corpo: "800 in hand, right now. Take it or leave it?"
aluguel_vencido.contrato_letra_miuda: Fine print: you end up owing {divida}.

brecho.sub: whatever the building left behind, she sells

oficina_zelador.fala: I even fix elevators here, kid. Bring the piece and some scrap and I'll get it right — up to +6.

caixa_dagua.intro: The valve on Rust's water tank sits in a tangle of pipes. Find the way without opening the wrong one — one mistake and the crew gets shocked, and the noise brings the janitor.

cena.boss_trancado: Lock the spots down before you level up, kid.
cena.nivel_rec_ocultar: don't warn me again in this hood
cena.nivel_rec_baixo: Recommended: crew at level {rec}. With gear counted, yours averages {atual} — you'll get wrecked. Run some jobs, level up on easier scraps, then come back.

aviso: Heads up, kid! Things just got hot.
Word is two guys on a bike are cruising the block, shaking everybody down.
Nobody's safe out here — not even us. If they find you, there's no talking.
The heat's on, kid! Cops in the area.
A patrol car's sweeping the Track for whoever's making noise.
Run if you want, but they know these streets better than you.
Bad news, kid. Your name got around.
A crew from another block crossed the line just to settle things with you.
Three of 'em. And they didn't come to talk.
The Bank's Collector is on the Track. Every crew pays its cut, and you owe yours.
He doesn't take excuses. He takes cash or blood.
They're sweeping the Market. Get caught and they take whatever's in your bag.
The Cats don't need light — they close in from every side.
The whole Market knows you owe.
The Turk's collectors came for a cut. Lose, and they take some of your cash.

cena.parada_ok: Nice. The street opened up for the crew.
cena.parada_falha: That went bad — and it woke folks up. Fight's coming.
cena.parada_falha_leve: Didn't stick this time. Next time, kid.
cena.corre_ok: Run done, no drama. Nato pays what was agreed, end of story.
cena.corre_falha: The patrol car clocked you. Drop the package and bounce, now!
cena.descanso_titulo: The crew rested. Each one recovered:
cena.descanso_ja_inteira: The crew's already whole, kid. Keep the cash.
cena.descanso_sem_grana: Cash is short for a rest, kid.
cena.tropa_no_chao: Your whole crew's down, kid. Nobody's facing anyone like this. Hit Nato's corner store first.
cena.aviso_rep_treta: That one's a whole different animal, kid. Don't go acting hard with no name made yet — stack up more rep before you step in there (rep {rep}).
cena.aviso_rep_clube: {agiota} won't even let you in the circle without a name on the street. Build more rep before you show up here (rep {rep}).

rep_recompensa.sub: Your name's ringing out on the street, kid. Go on, grab it.

cena.emprestimo_pedir: Take a loan (+{valor}, ends up owing {divida})
cena.emprestimo_contrato: {agiota} counts {valor} into your hand, doesn't even count it twice. "This one pays off, kid. Now you owe me {divida}. No deadline — just don't disappear."
cena.emprestimo_ja_deve: You already owe {agiota}, kid. Settle that before asking for more.
cena.fiado_pedir: Ask for more credit (heal everyone, ends up owing {divida})
cena.fiado_contrato_cura: {agiota} has your whole crew healed, on the tab. "Your debt doubled, kid. It's {divida} now."
cena.fiado_sem_emprestimo: You don't owe anything yet, kid. Take {agiota}'s loan first.
cena.fiado_teto: Your debt's maxed out, kid. {agiota}'s only fix now is throwing you into the pit.
cena.fiado_pago_total: Cleared the {pago}. Your name's clean with {agiota}.
cena.aviso_divida_chefe: {chefe} won't face you while you owe {agiota}, kid. Clear that {divida} debt first — his pit's the fastest way.
cena.clube_oferta_limpo: {agiota} looks you over. "You're clean with me. But I got a job: betting pit, mine. You go in, you win, you walk with {premio} in hand. No experience — nobody learns anything in the pit. You lose, we patch you up and you try again. Only the buy-in's on credit: I heal you now and it turns into debt if you don't win. Deal?"
cena.clube_oferta_divida: {agiota} taps the book. "You owe me. But I got a job for that: betting pit, mine. You go in, you win, your debt's gone — all of it, no matter the size. And you walk out with {premio} cash. No experience though — nobody learns a thing in the pit. You lose, we patch you up and you try again. The buy-in I float you — fifteen times — and I heal the whole crew. Deal?"

chegada: This is the Pista, kid. The asphalt down below — the root of it all.

Everybody worth something today crawled on this ground first. The Patchwork started here. A kid named Alan is going to start the same way, somewhere else — his turn just hasn't come yet. Now it's your turn to prove you're not just another face.

Take the kids' spots, get your name running mouth to mouth. When the whole Pista knows you exist, Coal comes down out of the dark to face you — and that's when you find out if you've got what it takes.
Move. Touch whatever's lighting up.

sinal.sub: kid selling candy, sharp eyes on everything
fala: Hey, you with the new gang? Came down to the Pista alone, no crew behind you. Either you're brave or you're stupid — I'll know real soon.
We don't just sell candy here, man. We sell what we see from this light. And we see EVERYTHING that moves on this block. Want to know something? Trade a word — or trade some cash.

compra.label: Buy the candy and hear what he saw
compra.resultado: He closes his fist on the change without even counting it. "The junkyard right up ahead. Old padlock, easy to crack. Inside there's scrap worth real money — and whatever the owner left before he vanished off the Pista for good."

aperta.label: Lean on the kid so he talks for free
resultado: The kid backs off but doesn't run. "Ugh, now it's really gone bad. Should've bought the candy."
"You lean on a kid like that and then want respect? Not happening." He whistles — and he's not alone.

ignora.label: Ignore him and keep climbing
ignora.resultado: You walk past without even a glance. The kid spits and burns your face into memory — information's a currency too, and now he owes you one. There's a junkyard up ahead.

ferro.sub: locked gate, a secret kept inside
ferro.intro: The gate's just a chain with a combination lock — nothing a trained hand can't handle. The crew watches the pins turn once, then it's memorize the sequence and repeat it without a shake. Slip a hand and the guard wakes up and the game turns into a fight on the spot.

fala: This alley's Rato de Pista, pal. We don't want to climb, don't want your turf, don't want to own anything — we just don't want to get stepped on. And a fresh gang coming down here thinking it owns the street... this one gets stepped on, no tears.
Well, look who's here. Fresh little crew thinking the Pista's a playground.
This face again? Maybe this time you learn.

rinha.sub: endless fights — even with the app closed
rinha.fala: Betting ring at the back of the alley, kid. You step in, you eat it or you cash out. There's always some nutcase wanting to test their hand against the fresh gang — come on, take it as many times as you can stay standing. The ring never stops here: one's done, the next steps in — weaker, stronger, luck of the draw. You can leave the crew here and go live your life: 1 brawl every 5 minutes.

birosca.sub: the corner elder — the only grown-up on the Pista you can trust
fala: Sit, kid. Have some mate. You're climbing way too fast for someone nobody around here knows by name.
I know where Coal hides when he vanishes into the dark. I'll tell you, no runaround. But first do me a run — take a package across without the patrol car's beam catching your trail.
Handle that and the Pista starts to respect you, not just fear you. And the bar keeps its door open for your crew to rest whenever it needs to.

aceita_corre.label: Take Nato's run
aceita_corre.resultado: "Done, kid. Package is behind the counter. And a bonus: Rasteira's other spot is right up to the right."

so_papo.label: Just want the information
so_papo.resultado: "Stubborn, huh. Then straight to the bone: Rasteira's other spot is up there. Lock both down and Coal shows up on his own, wanting to know who you are."

informante.sub: knows everything that moves in Marélia before it's a rumor
fala: Hey, back on the Pista? That's what this block is: everything that happens in Marélia passes through here before it's even corner gossip. And I hear ALL of it, kid.
There's something going on over at the Feira the folks there won't tell you for free. The Collector's lying low, waiting for the right moment to show.

perguntar.label: Ask about the Feira
perguntar.resultado: "The Collector only comes out of hiding once he knows his enforcers already took a beating. Go to the Feira, handle the spots — then come back if you need more intel."

corre.sub: carry the package without the patrol car seeing
corre.intro: Cross the block with the package without stepping into the patrol car's beam — one wrong turn and it's a sure fight with a badge. The crew spreads out and covers your move. It's the price of Nato's information, and also the price of peace here on the Pista.

beco_2.fala: You again? Took the alley down there and already figured the whole Pista would kneel for the fresh gang. Changes hands every week here, man — but not for whoever shows up thinking they own a corner on day one.

descanso.intro: Some time sitting, out of the hot street sun, in Nato's bar. Costs a little change, but it patches the crew up and everyone comes back whole — hurt, nobody wins a fight.

descanso_2.sub: on the other side of the wall
descanso_2.intro: Nato's cousin runs a makeshift bar over on this side. Same deal: pay a little change and the crew sorts itself out before heading into Carvão's warehouse.

fala: Psst. Need quick cash, kid? I lend 100. That's it — don't push for more.
100 in your hand, right now. We settle up later — just don't come with excuses.
agiota.contrato_corpo: "100 in your hand, right now. You in or out?"
agiota.contrato_letra_miuda: Fine print of the deal: you end up owing {divida}.

fala: "You lost your mind coming here, huh?" Carvão's first crew blocks the way.
Two heavy dealers smoking on the warehouse steps. They spot you and spit on the ground.
Carvão's right hand in person, with an escort. "Past the wall, you come in by invitation. Were you invited?"
This one doesn't run. Folds his arms, signals the goons: "handle it."

achado.linha: Behind a pile of scrap, a forgotten crate: some change and iron that still works. Nobody will miss it — the owner's long gone, vanished off the Pista, and nobody asks why.

fala: You beat the kids and already figured the Pista was yours? I trained every one of these punks with my own hands. Face me first — then Coal comes down to see you up close.
Trained every one of these kids with these hands. Come see what's left to teach you.
Back? Good. Now I get to teach it again, with more feeling.

oficina.sub: Mr. Nando fixes what the street breaks
fala: Look at the fresh little gang already working the spots. Let me tell you something, kid: to face Coal you need iron in your hand, not just chest.
Bring me two pieces of scrap from that junkyard — one you pull cracking the lock, the other's hidden in the back. Bring them and I'll forge you a piece on the spot for your crew.
And as a bonus I'll drop where Coal hides when he vanishes into the dark. That's worth more than any weapon, kid. We got a deal?

forjar.label: Hand over the scrap and take the piece
forjar.resultado: Nando hammers a while, blows off the smoke and passes you a still-warm tin knuckle. "Coal parks deep in Rasteira's alley, behind the wall. Vanishes in the dark, but always to the same corner — a crook always repeats a pattern. Now go up and get him."

beco_3.sub: another piece of Rato de Pista
beco_3.fala: You people don't quit, huh? The Pista's got spots like bullet holes — there's always one more hidden in some corner. This one's mine. Come prove you're worth it, or go back where you came from.

sinaleiro.sub: if he whistles, the whole block runs
fala: I run the eyes of the whole Pista, kid. Every lookout, every signal, every runner at the light answers to my whistle. You got past all of them without anyone whistling — but you don't get past me. With me it's different.
I whistle, the whole block runs to help. Who do you whistle to?
Thought it'd be easy the second time? Wrong, kid.

predio.tunel_ent: Shack at the end of the alley
predio.tunel_sai: Shack on the other side of the wall

fala: Look at the fresh gang's kids trying to walk into the warehouse like it's nothing. No playboys who think they own the place in here, kid. This is the real thing.
No playboys in here, kid. This is bone.
Past the dock? Lucky I was sleeping light. Wake up now, 'cause the fight already started.
Dozed off a second and look what's left to beat on.
This time I was waiting, see. Come on.

achado.linha: Back of the shelf, under some old rags: something useful. Nobody's going to notice it's gone.

contador.sub: keeps every tally, takes a beating for anyone
fala: Don't hit me, kid! I just do the math, I swear to God! I'll talk, I'll talk, all of it...
Coal stays in the dark, way in the back of it all. He only comes down once the whole warehouse knows you're here. And guess what — it knows.

escuta.label: Hear him out
escuta.resultado: "That board back there is the operation schedule, for real. Coal crosses the last room every dawn, same time always. Good luck, kid — you'll need it."

fala: Nobody goes down this hole without going through me first, kid. Back to your side while you still can.
This hole's mine, kid. Nobody passes for free.
Still trying this gap? You really are stubborn.
You really think you're the first to try digging under? The ones who tried before are still down here in the dark, no way out.
This hole's mine, kid. Nobody passes for free.
Still trying this gap? You really are stubborn.
Made it to the other side, huh? Only over me, kid. And I don't go down easy.
This hole's mine, kid. Nobody passes for free.
Still trying this gap? You really are stubborn.

achado.linha: Jammed into a crack in the dirt wall, half hidden: something that still works for the crew.

banca.fala: "Nobody gets beat up here, kid. Here you bet. Sharp head wins, sharp hands win — and whoever knows fighting reads the pit before the first punch."

bancada_nando.fala: Bring the piece and some scrap and I'll hammer it right. A weapon that hit soft now and then hits solid every time after I'm done.

cena.hint_andar: Use the stick and head down to the street.
cena.hint_interagir: You hit a hot spot — press INTERACT.
cena.hint_sucata: 🔩 Take both scrap pieces to Nando at the workshop. He'll sort you out.
cena.hint_sucata_falta: 🔩 You're missing a scrap piece — it's in the back of the junkyard. Grab both and take them to Nando.
cena.muro_tunel: The wall's not opening, straight up. Find the gap under it.
cena.checklist_dica: Close all of this and the gap under the wall opens — that's how you reach Carvão.
cena.checklist_tunel_aberto: The gap is open. Head to the shack against the wall and go down. Carvão is an even fight at level 15 — if your crew is below that, grind a few fights first.
cena.checklist_dominada: Strip's yours. The wall's open now, come and go as you please.
cena.descanso_completo: Full recovery: health, downed and status (−{grana})
cena.agiota_socorro_fala: {agiota} shakes his head. "Enough, kid. That debt's past what I can even collect. I'll patch you up for free — but you're settling this in the pit, like it or not."

chegada: This is the Market, kid. No gunfire here — just bills.
Every stall pays the Turk, and every cent is in his ledger. The upper half is pitch dark: the Cats cut the power.
Want the Collector? Make the whole Market respect you first.
feira.aviso_informante: The Collector won't even see you yet. Someone back on the Track knows the way in — talk to Duda.
feira.boss_trancado: The blackout barricade is shut — sort out the lower Market first.
feira.muro_passagem: The barricade won't open — but the Cats' Gallery runs underneath.
feira.checklist_dica: Clear everything down here to open the Cats' Gallery.
feira.checklist_passagem: Gallery open — cross to the dark side.
feira.hint_radio_pronto: You've got the copper and all 3 valves — take them to Toninho to fix the radio.
feira.hint_radio_falta: Toninho's radio needs 1 copper wire and 3 valves. Search the Market (the street vendor sells one).

catraca.sub: the Cats' toll at the entrance
fala: Whoa, whoa. Market entry isn't free, pal.
Pay the change or get through us.

banca_turco.sub: where the Market pays its dues
fala: New crew in the Market... The Turk likes new people. New people still pay on time.
Arrival fee: 20. Pay and you're cool. Don't, and the Collector comes to chat.
fala_devedor: Look who's here. You're in the ledger, huh? Owing the loan shark and still wanting a stall.
Pay the arrival fee or the collectors find you before you find the exit.

paga_taxa.label: Pay the 20 fee
paga_taxa.resultado: He writes your name down neatly. "A payer. The Turk likes that. His collectors don't like anyone, though — they're right over there."

nao_paga.label: Pay nothing
nao_paga.resultado: He closes the ledger slowly. "Noted. Go talk to the collectors, then."

fala: We came for what's the Turk's.
Everybody pays. You'll pay too — one way or another.

quadro_luz.sub: the tap that feeds the Market
quadro_luz.intro: The Cats pull power for the whole Market from this box. Retrace the wires without touching the live ones — one mistake and the crew gets shocked, and the noise brings the gang.

fala: You messed with our box? Nobody touches our power.
The Cats live in the dark, pal. Come learn how it feels.
I do the weighing here. And I weighed you: you owe.
Every stall pays whatever weight I say.
I know the name of every debtor in Marélia. Yours is right here.
Debtors get beaten with interest.
The pirate radio talked about me, huh? Then you know who I am.
I'm the hand the Turk uses to settle accounts.
Everything the Market pays goes through me.
Want the cash? Come take it out of the safe.
This radio picks up the Settling Scores frequency — the Turk's guys talk about everything on it.
Only it's fried. Bring me 1 copper wire and 3 valves and I'll make it talk.

consertar.label: Hand over the copper and 3 valves
consertar.resultado: Toninho solders, blows, turns the knob... and the radio crackles out a voice: "The Hand and the Strongbox are in the Market today." Now you know where they are.

camelo.sub: a bit of everything, cheaper if you can talk

muamba.sub: cross the Market without the Raid seeing
muamba.intro: Carry the goods from one end of the Market to the other. The Raid is patrolling and the clock is ticking — get spotted and you lose it all.

favor_marmita.intro: Dona Regina asked: take her son's lunchbox to the other side of the Market without the Raid seizing it. Favor paid means credit's open again.

favor_devedor.sub: has owed Dona Regina for months
fala: What? Regina sent you? I'll pay next week, I swear.
Next week, same as last week.

convence.label: Talk him into it
convence.resultado: He scratches his head, sighs and pays Regina. "Fine, fine. She always fed me anyway."

aperta.label: Lean on him
aperta.resultado: He backs off and calls his buddies. "Came to collect with your fists? Then take some fists."

fala: The old lady owes the Turk. Out of the way.
Wanna pay for her? Pay in bruises.

pagina_1.linha: Stuck to the floor of a stall: a page from the Turk's ledger, full of names and numbers. There are more around.

pagina_2.linha: On the dark side, folded in a crate: another ledger page. There's a note from the Collector in the margin.

pagina_3.linha: Hidden in the Cats' Gallery: the last page. Together they show where the Collector is weak — he drops his guard when he collects.

fala: The radio crackles in the corner of the shop. Between the static, a voice talks about the Lowside.
"...down there the Gut-Stabber runs things. Anyone who wants to reach him has to listen first..."

ouvir.label: Listen to the whole frequency
ouvir.resultado: You write down everything the radio said about the Lowside. When the time comes, you'll know the way in.

pensao.sub: hot food and a clean bed
pensao.intro: Dona Regina serves a plate of food and settles the crew in a corner. Costs a bit of cash — and if you're broke, she finds another way.
pensao.favor_pedir: Broke — ask for credit in exchange for a favor
pensao.favor_pendente: You still owe Regina a favor
pensao.favor_fala: "Eat, kid. Later you do me a favor — the Market is full of people who owe me."

pensao_2.sub: Regina's daughter, on the dark side
pensao_2.intro: Dona Regina's daughter runs a boarding house on the dark side, by candlelight. Same rule as her mom: pay a bit and the crew gets patched up.
pensao_2.favor_pedir: Broke — ask for credit in exchange for a favor
pensao_2.favor_pendente: You still owe Regina a favor
pensao_2.favor_fala: "My mom told me about you. Eat up — settle the favor with her."

fala: Need big money, kid? I don't do small change.
300 in hand right now. But the bill... the bill is mine.
juro_alto.contrato_corpo: "300 in hand, right now. Take it or leave it?"

fala: Past here is the Wholesale Market. Nobody passes without paying.
And you can't afford what we charge.

deposito_2.sub: only opens for people with a name
fala: You got a name in the Market? Prove it.
The Turk only sees people the street respects.
Out here in the dark the ring never stops spinning.
Step in and take the hits. This is where you grind, not where you get rich.
The ring never stops: one's done, the next one steps in, drawn at random. You can leave the crew here — 1 brawl every 5 minutes.

serralheria.fala: Nando does the first tune-up. I go all the way: bring the piece and scrap and I'll have it hitting hard every time.

fala: Came into the Gallery? This is the Cats' house, pal.
Nobody crosses without paying the toll.

porta.intro: An iron door with a code lock. The Cats change the password every week — crack the code to get through. Get it wrong and they'll come check who touched it.

fala: You opened our door? Now you're stuck in here with us.
In the dark we see better than you.
Almost out, huh? Almost.
The light is on the other side of me.
The cold room is for dead meat. You're staying here.
I guard what's the Turk's. You don't pass.

achado.sub: what the Turk keeps for himself
achado.linha: Behind the merchandise boxes: cash, scrap and a good piece. The Turk won't notice — he never counts his own stock.

fala: On the desk, the Turk's cash book. Every stall, every debtor, every cent.
On the last sheet, a note from the Collector: "when I collect, I drop my guard".

ler.label: Read it all
ler.resultado: You close the book. Gather the 3 ledger pages and the Collector steps into the fight with his guard down.

fala: You took the wrong aisle into the Wholesale Market, pal. Every stall in here is the Turk's.
Wanna pass? Pay the canvas toll — in bruises.
Hey, hey, hey! Call the boys, there's an intruder between the stalls!
In here we fight as a pack, kid. Alone, you don't get out.
This maze was built so nobody finds the safe.
And whoever finds it gets beat by me first.
Every stall you pass is a debt you make, you know?
I'm collecting this one right now.
You made it far, huh. All the Turk's collectors in one place.
From here on, only people who settle up get through.
After me there's just Sledge and the safe.
And you won't see either one.

briga_auto_aviso.titulo: AUTO BRAWL // YOU BUMPED, NOW IT'S ON
frases: Went looking for smoke? Well, you found it. Brace yourself!
Rolled up talking tough? Now you gotta back it up.
Uh-oh, bad luck: his crew's already closing in.
No chickening out, homie — it's hands now.
Bumped the wrong hardhead, kid. Go in heavy!
Nowhere left to run. Throw down!
Yikes… this one didn't come to talk. Gotta go in heavy.
You went looking for trouble. Trouble looked back.

fala: You wanna go to the Projects? Kid, those are ten-floor towers, and every floor has an owner.
My nephew lives on the fifth. Says Rust lives way up top, and nobody ever reached him without taking a beating on every flight.

ouvir.label: Hear everything about the Projects
ouvir.resultado: She tells you about the front desk, the padlock, the unlit stairwell and Dona Neide on the fifth floor. When the time comes, you know who to look for.

chegada: This is the Lowside, kid. The other side of the train tracks.
When Shadow went into the ditch, his crew split in three: Sangria, Ice and Leftover. There's a loudmouth here who says he runs it all — calls himself Gut-Stabber and never stops running.
Nobody respects you for free here. Every fight you win is respect in your account.
And watch the train: when it whistles, get off the tracks.
baixada.aviso_informante: Nobody in the Lowside will take you to the boss yet. The Market's pirate radio knows the way — listen to it first.
baixada.checklist_dica: Earn the Lowside's respect: beat the loudmouth until he's got nowhere left to run.
baixada.checklist_passagem: The old man woke up. Go to the entrance and face the real owner of the Lowside.
baixada.hint_cafe_falta: The loudmouth spilled it: the Lowside's owner is the old man at the entrance. Get a coffee at Dona Cida's bakery.
baixada.hint_cafe_pronto: Coffee in hand. Take it to the old man at the entrance.
baixada.trem_atropelo: The train brushed past — the crew took a hit and got thrown off the tracks.
baixada.respeito_falta: {n} more before the loudmouth stops running
baixada.respeito_cheio: respect full — the loudmouth has nowhere left to run

veio.nome: The old man at the entrance
fala: The red sky against the blue world, you feel me? Think about that.
The blind man saw what the deaf man heard, partner. And nobody believed either of them.
A train that passes doesn't come back… but the tracks stay, you feel me?
Whoever runs too much gets to the wrong place early.
Ants have no boss and the anthill never falls. Think about that, partner.
Coffee gets cold. Respect doesn't.
You think you're climbing the street, but the street's the one taking you down.
A big name in a small mouth weighs nothing, kid.
I've been the ditch and I've been the bridge. Today I'm the curb.

veio_cafe.nome: The old man at the entrance
veio_cafe.sub: his nose already caught the smell
fala: Hm… what's that smell? Been a long time since anyone brought me a real coffee…

dar_cafe.label: Hand the old man the coffee
dar_cafe.resultado: He drinks it in one gulp. Blinks. His eyes clear — and suddenly there's no groggy old man there anymore. He stands up slowly, cracks his neck and stares you down.

folgado_1.sub: the loudmouth who runs the Lowside — or so he says
fala: I'm Gut-Stabber, I own this place. You're not even worth my time.
Bloodletter! Handle this punk for me. I've got better things to do.

folgado_2.sub: ran to the other side of the tracks
fala: You again? I don't waste my time on nobodies.
Ice, deal with him. I'm busy being important.
Look, you're starting to get on my nerves.
Leftover! Where's Leftover? Get the Scraps over here, now!
Fine, fine. You're stubborn. But you won't handle the Biggest Shard.
Take care of it, Shard. I'm gonna… go over there. Take care of something.
Nobody beats Shadow's Name. Nobody!
If you get past him… no, you're not getting past him.
Okay… okay. It's you and me now. I'm Gut-Stabber! I… I think.
Come on, I'm tough. Real tough. Super tough, honest.

dona_cida.sub: the bakery that opens before the sun
fala: Peacock came running in here, all bruised, saying his name isn't Gut-Stabber at all.
The real Gut-Stabber is Old Bucho, kid. The old man at the entrance. He's been like that a long time… only a strong coffee will wake him up.

pega_cafe.label: Take the old man's coffee
pega_cafe.resultado: She pours it through the cloth filter, bottles it and hands it over. "Take it hot. Cold won't wake him."

fala: The Lowside's circle never stops, not even when the train goes by.
One ends, another steps in, random. You can leave your crew here — 1 fight every 5 minutes.

caixa_trilho.linha: A dented crate dumped on the gravel: some cash and a bottle of syrup nobody came back for.

birosca.intro: Dona Lurdes sets the crew up in the back, away from the train noise. Costs a little and everyone walks out whole.

birosca_2.sub: a bed on the other side of the tracks
birosca_2.intro: A cramped room overlooking the rails. Not pretty, but the crew sleeps and gets back to the grind.

fala: Need cash? In the Lowside money's got three owners, and I collect for all three.
500 in your hand now. The bill… I'll tell you the bill later.
taxa_fixa.contrato_corpo: "500 in hand, right now. Take it or leave it?"

enemy_album.1701: Rides the stick-up bike. Never gets off, just revs — the backseat does the talking.
enemy_album.1702: Rides on the back and calls the stick-up. "Nobody's safe."
enemy_album.1711: Works the late-night patrol. Frisks anyone still on the street after ten.
enemy_album.1712: Runs the patrol car. Doesn't want explanations, wants ID.
enemy_album.1101: Doesn't fight, he runs and warns — facing him is a chase before a beating.
enemy_album.1102: The corner's eye — clocks everything moving on the Track, and comments on all of it.
enemy_album.1103: The fastest on the Track — bolts after two hits in a row.
enemy_album.1104: One of the boldest Cats, taps even a watched pole.
enemy_album.1105: A debtor turned thug to pay off his own debt.
enemy_album.1106: Light stun shock — the Market's living alarm.
enemy_album.1107: The youngest of the shards, still proving himself.
enemy_album.1108: Attacks timed to the passing train.
enemy_album.1109: Spreads a rumor about a rival before the fight.
enemy_album.1110: Watches the main door, warns the whole crew.
enemy_album.1111: Patrols the dark stairwell, uses the light as a weapon.
enemy_album.1112: Fights over any small thing, always on edge.
enemy_album.1113: Hits from range before you get close.
enemy_album.1115: Knows every hidden path on the Hill.
enemy_album.1116: Literal door guard, never leaves the post.
enemy_album.1118: Owes the Accountant, fights to pay it off.
enemy_album.1119: Last step before the sewing room — nothing passes unseen.
enemy_album.1120: Sees all that comes and goes on the Roof, reports straight to the Patchwork.
enemy_album.1121: Spots all of Marélia before any attack lands.
enemy_album.1201: Corner kids — the first real scrap.
enemy_album.1202: Copied Coal until the nickname stuck.
enemy_album.1203: Dirty fighter, fast hits, low damage.
enemy_album.1204: Runs illegal power hookups — vanishes among the stalls.
enemy_album.1205: Works the stall by day, collects by night.
enemy_album.1206: Collects an old debt only he remembers.
enemy_album.1207: Devotee of the dead Shadow, still "talks to him".
enemy_album.1208: Recycles weapons from junk — unpredictable damage.
enemy_album.1209: Lives near where the Shadow fell, the others avoid him.
enemy_album.1210: Strangles with a clothesline, improvised weapon.
enemy_album.1211: Access to every unit, valuable information.
enemy_album.1212: Undercover — looks like an ordinary resident.
enemy_album.1213: Uses the Hill's slope as a weapon.
enemy_album.1215: One of the kids she raised, borrowed technique.
enemy_album.1216: Always fights in a pair, never alone.
enemy_album.1217: Punishes anyone who breaks the Wheel's formation.
enemy_album.1218: Recruits and trains for the Five.
enemy_album.1219: Freshly recruited, still proving himself to the crew.
enemy_album.1220: The only stash left up top — small, symbolic.
enemy_album.1221: Sells the sewing scraps — literal patchwork.
enemy_album.1301: Aggressive, a step above the common kids.
enemy_album.1302: Scars from those who lost to him — war trophies.
enemy_album.1303: Steals what he sees, won't let go of what he grabs.
enemy_album.1304: Street collector — hits before the boss really collects.
enemy_album.1305: Knows what every resident owes, uses it as a mind game.
enemy_album.1307: Claims to be the rightful successor, no one agrees.
enemy_album.1308: The angriest of the Shadow's three shards.
enemy_album.1312: Only attacks in tight space, dirty hallway fighting.
enemy_album.1313: Stairway watch with say over who climbs.
enemy_album.1314: Captain — rose fast, hits harder than anyone.
enemy_album.1315: Guards the last bend before the Upper Hill.
enemy_album.1316: One of the five who nearly became a council.
enemy_album.1317: Right hand of the near-formed council.
enemy_album.1318: Fights in formation, protects the center.
enemy_album.1319: Front line of the Patchwork's crew.
enemy_album.1320: Second line, trusted with half the Roof.
enemy_album.1401: A candy seller with a rock in his pocket.
enemy_album.1402: Collects to the last coin, never miscounts.
enemy_album.1403: Trusted muscle, collects big debts without talk.
enemy_album.1404: Doubles the debt if the deadline slips.
enemy_album.1405: The most desperate shard — nothing to lose.
enemy_album.1406: Collects for all three shards at once.
enemy_album.1407: Looks down on the crew from above.
enemy_album.1408: Collects the "rent" the crew imposes on every floor.
enemy_album.1409: Fires a warning, doesn't mind hitting you.
enemy_album.1410: Keeps the books on who owes Zefa a favor.
enemy_album.1411: The most ambitious of the Five.
enemy_album.1414: Closes the account of anyone climbing without paying the toll.
enemy_album.1451: Commands every lookout — if he whistles, the block runs.
enemy_album.1452: The oldest of the Signal Crew, trained the kids.
enemy_album.1453: The Collector's right hand, handles what he won't touch.
enemy_album.1455: The most respected shard, nearly reunited the Lowside alone.
enemy_album.1456: Uses the dead boss's name as a weapon.
enemy_album.1457: Runs a whole building by himself.
enemy_album.1458: Access to every unit — info worth more than cash.
enemy_album.1459: Minds the kids when Zefa can't.
enemy_album.1460: Controls the climb alone, no one passes without a nod.
enemy_album.1461: One of the Five closest to a real council seat.
enemy_album.1462: Leads the Wheel in battle — doctrine made flesh.
enemy_album.1463: General — runs the whole Roof for the Patchwork.
enemy_album.1464: Scissors' right hand, never misses the final cut.
enemy_album.1500: Vanishes mid-street, strikes in the dark. Boss of the Track.
enemy_album.1501: Logs everything, collects everything. Breaks an arm before the face.
enemy_album.1502: Took the whole Lowsides when the Shadow fell in the ditch.
enemy_album.1503: Lives on the tenth floor — you arrive already tired.
enemy_album.1504: Raised half the kids around here. Knows where to hit to hurt without harm.
enemy_album.1505: Doesn't fight out of anger — fights because the math works out.
enemy_album.1600: The only one who ever held six blocks at once.
enemy_album.1322: The loudmouth who called himself Gut-Stabber. A boss's swagger, an extra's punch.

album.sub: Everything your gang has seen, beaten and picked up in Marélia.
album.item_dica_loja: Buy it at a turf shop.
album.item_dica_drop: Drop — from a boss or a fight.
album.item_dica_quest: Earned by running a favor for the block.
album.cartas_explica: Every card drops from its own enemy. Slotted into gear, it stays forever.

1.desc: Half Pace — takes twice as long to get a turn.

2.desc: Loses 1 Grit every turn. Never knocks out: stops at 1.

5.desc: Asleep on their feet: loses the turn (1 to 3 times). Wakes up when hit.

6.desc: Drank something spiked: loses 1/8 of max Grit every turn. Stops at 1.

7.desc: Can't tell who's who: 1 in 3 chance to hit a partner (or themselves).

8.desc: Body locked up: half Pace and 1 in 4 chance to lose the turn.

9.desc: Burning: loses a little Grit every turn and hits with −2 Wallop. Stops at 1.

gangues.log_perdeu_vez_apagado: 💤 {nome} is out cold and lost the turn.
gangues.log_perdeu_vez_travado: ⚡ {nome} seized up and lost the turn.

banca.sem_grana: No cash to bet right now.
banca.desafio_intro: Pick the stake and the difficulty. Uncle Dice draws the game. Solve it, take the prize; miss it, the cash stays on the table.
banca.desafio_jogando: Playing for {valor} — solve it and take {premio}.
banca.rinha_intro: Two from the street are about to scrap on their own. Pick who you're backing: the odds are what each 1 cash pays.
banca.perdeu: You lost {n}. The house thanks you.

farm_ausente.calculando: Counting what went down on the street…
farm_ausente.teto: Hit the +5 levels cap for one absence — from here on, you gotta play.
farm_ausente.derrota: The crew went down with no cash to patch up: the pit is over, you got dragged to the bar and every auto switched off.
farm_ausente.pouco_tempo: Under 5 minutes at the pit — it closes 1 brawl every 5 minutes, and this one didn't make it.
farm_ausente.meio_nao_conta: The brawl that was going on when you came back didn't finish in time — that one doesn't count.
farm_ausente.remendos: Lost {n}× with cash on hand: the house charged the patch-up and the pit kept going.

ferreiro.regra: Each upgrade takes the luck out of the gear: odd levels roll the die twice and keep the higher (▲), even levels raise the minimum. At the cap, it always hits the max.
ferreiro.vazio: No gear in the crew can be upgraded — only weapon, head, hands, feet and amulet pieces with a range.
ferreiro.feito: {nome} is +{n} now. You'll feel it in your hand.
ferreiro.falta_teto: I can't push that one any further.
ferreiro.falta_sucata: Not enough scrap. No iron, no miracles.

gangues.log_item_em: {nome} handed {item} to {alvo} ({efeito}) — gave up the attack.
gangues.log_item_inimigos: {nome} threw {item} at the crew ({efeito}) — gave up the attack.

itens_efeito.material: repair material — not used in fights

lore.1: A little unlabeled bottle the gas-station auntie swears is cough syrup. Nobody asks what's inside. It works.
lore.2: Blue water in a reused bottle. Legend says it's from the same tap Old Nego washed his face at before a fight.
lore.3: Rolled in corn husk, thick smoke. Calms the head and leaves the guard loose — the price of any calm on the street.
lore.4: Dented can, tastes like a battery. Whoever drinks it doesn't sleep; whoever doesn't sleep doesn't miss a turn.
lore.5: A strip of old T-shirt torn on the spot. It's no hospital, but it holds the blood till the next corner.
lore.6: From the corner bottle at Mr. Zé's bar. Gives courage to spare and takes judgment in equal measure.
lore.8: A June-festival firecracker with extra powder. It pops, it stinks, and nobody sees a thing for a moment.
lore.10: Flour with powdered guarana, the recipe of whoever trains in the alley. Sits heavy and raises the dead.
lore.11: Lit in the corner of the Hill's church. It doesn't stop punches, but the crew believes it does — sometimes that's enough.
lore.12: A one-real bag of candy from the trailer. Pure sugar for anyone seeing stars.
lore.13: Bolts, springs, a bit of pipe. To anyone else it's junk; to Bigode at the metal shop it's raw material.
lore.14: Wire yanked off a pole in the dark. Worth more than it looks, and gets you more jail time than it looks, too.
lore.15: An old radio valve, still warm from use. Only good for someone who knows how to fix what the world threw away.
lore.20: A scraped bottle cap stamped with a fist. Whoever keeps one says it carries the punch of a brute who fell on the Track.
lore.21: An arcade token with a wall scratched in by pocketknife. It takes one hit like it was brick.
lore.22: An empty lighter with a chip glued on. Nobody knows how it works. Nobody wants to be in front when it does.
lore.30: A bag of ice from the fish stall, wrapped round a twisted ankle. Whoever was dazed starts seeing again.
lore.31: A gauze roll bought on credit at the pharmacy. Stops the cut and the shame of bleeding in front of everyone.
lore.32: Cloth-filter coffee, black as the small hours. A limp arm lifts on the first sip.
lore.33: The ointment grandma rubbed on everything. Closes an open guard and leaves you smelling like home.
lore.34: A glass bottle of root, honey and prayer. Grandma never told the recipe, and nobody dared ask twice.
lore.35: A bucket from the laundry sink thrown in the face of whoever blacked out. Rude, effective, very street.
lore.36: Hot milk with cinnamon, to wash a hex out of the body. Grandma said spells don't like milk.
lore.37: A glass of water with three spoons of sugar. The universal cure for anyone groggy from a scare or a punch.
lore.38: A pharmacy patch that heats like crazy. Unlocks a stuck joint, and a stuck curse word too.
lore.39: An aloe leaf from the rooftop pot. Cut, squeeze, spread. The burn fades; the scar stays to tell the story.
lore.201: Ripped off mom's broom in the middle of an argument. She still wants it back.
lore.202: Flat brim, sticker still on. On the Track, whoever peels the sticker off didn't buy it.
lore.203: Tore in the first fight, stayed on in the second out of pride. Now it's a uniform.
lore.204: A wrap round the fist like a garage-gym boxer. Doesn't protect much, but it commands respect.
lore.205: Hole at the big toe, sole peeling off. Outran a lot of cops and never got caught.
lore.206: Gold-painted tin chain from a street vendor. Shines from afar, rusts up close.
lore.207: Real brass knuckles, turned on the lathe of someone who wouldn't give a name. Leaves marks that don't fade.
lore.208: Black cloth with the crew's symbol. Whoever wears it never walks alone, even when they do.
lore.209: Genuine leather, smells like an old motorbike. They say it belonged to a courier who vanished at the Market.
lore.210: A tennis wristband from a tournament nobody played. Steadies the wrist so the punch comes out faster.
lore.211: Army boot from a thrift store. It's kicked in more doors than its owner remembers.
lore.212: A real gold tooth — or close enough. A smile that warns: this one's been beaten and came back.
lore.213: A stub of construction pipe, short enough to hide in your pants. It's not a weapon, it's an argument.
lore.214: A faded fleece beanie. Keeps the head warm and hides the face at the right moment.
lore.215: A safety vest with magazines stuffed inside. Neighborhood engineering.
lore.216: A bricklayer's leather glove. It's held bricks, sledgehammers and the collar of plenty of loudmouths.
lore.217: Flip-flop with a tire sole sewn on. Won't slip even on a wet market floor.
lore.218: A saint's medal passed from father to son. Protects the body — and the family name.
lore.219: A manhole cover pried off a Market street. Heavy, ugly, and nothing gets past it.
lore.220: A yellow hard hat from a site stalled for ten years. The building never went up, but the hat took plenty of blows.
lore.221: Metal plates wired onto an old vest. Noisy, but no knife gets through.
lore.222: A strip of truck tire strapped to the forearm. Hits it and bounces back.
lore.223: Factory boot with a steel toe. Steps on nails, steps on people, feels nothing.
lore.224: A wooden-bead rosary, worn smooth by prayer. Grandma prayed for you before you were born.
lore.225: A black candle only lit at crossroads. Whoever snuffs it early pays for it later.
lore.226: A threadbare hood that's hidden three generations of folk healers. It keeps more secrets than the head inside it.
lore.227: Printed cloth bought at the last stall of the Market. The seller didn't charge, just said: "it chose you".
lore.228: Beads of every color, one for each saint. It snapped once and its owner didn't leave home for a month.
lore.229: A raw-leather sandal, handmade. Steps light, leaves no one's footprints.
lore.230: A bead necklace washed in waterfall water. Whoever wears it hears a little more than everyone else.
lore.231: A guava branch from a prayer-woman's backyard. Looks silly until someone takes a hit from it.
lore.232: A turban tied the old way. Keeps your thoughts in place when the fight gets ugly.
lore.233: A raw-cloth mantle embroidered in red thread. They say whoever wears it feels the street breathing.
lore.234: A ring carved from coconut shell. When it warms on your finger, it's a warning: envy's close by.
lore.235: A flip-flop that went through seven blessings. It won't step on an offering — it swerves on its own.
lore.236: A blue glass eye from far away. It looks back at whoever gives you the evil eye.
lore.237: Knuckles made from a crushed paint can. Every kid's first weapon, the day they thought they were grown.
lore.238: A cap found at the bus stop. No owner, no brand, no shame.
lore.138: The club the Collector used to settle accounts at the Market. Every notch in the wood is a debt someone paid with their teeth.
lore.139: The machete Coal wore at his hip and never needed to draw. When you draw it, the whole Track goes quiet.
lore.16: Poured through Dona Cida's cloth filter, strong as a punch. Wakes up even someone who's been asleep for years.
lore.140: The skewer Gut-Stabber never let go of, not even asleep. Whoever holds it feels the weight of the whole Lowside.
lore.301: Pulled off a rooftop grill in the middle of Sunday lunch. Still smells like charcoal.
lore.302: A black hood for someone who doesn't want to be remembered. In the Lowside, vanishing is a talent.
lore.303: A leather vest studded with old belt rivets. Each stud is from a fight its owner won.
lore.304: A glove from a gym that shut down. The padding's gone, the anger stayed.
lore.305: The brand's misspelled, but it runs just the same. Nobody in the Lowside asks where it came from.
lore.306: Real silver — so they say. It jingles when its owner walks, and everyone knows he's arrived.
lore.307: The fridge door that broke in '98. Doesn't keep anything cold, but it takes a punch beautifully.
lore.308: A courier's helmet with a half-peeled Shadow sticker. It's saved more heads than a lot of doctors.
lore.309: Chunks of truck tire sewn into a vest. Heavy, smelly, and nothing gets through.
lore.310: PVC pipe cut and strapped to the arm. Cheap, ugly, works.
lore.311: A work boot with the steel toe poking through. Step on a show-off's foot and the message is sent.
lore.312: A wooden fig hand tied to a sprig of rue. Grandma said the evil eye doesn't get past it.
lore.313: A dried, braided rue branch. Where it hits, it leaves a smell nobody forgets.
lore.314: A straw hat that's been through three terreiros. Shades you from the sun and from the hex.
lore.315: Flowered calico hand-sewn by the trackside healer. Whoever wears it feels the ground shake before the train.
lore.316: Three knots, three wishes. It can only break on its own — and when it does, the wish comes true.
lore.317: A rope sandal the healer wore until it wore out. Steps light and leaves the street silent.
lore.318: A little leather pouch sewn shut with a prayer inside. Nobody opens it, nobody asks, everybody respects it.
